chunks: And from him (Al-Hilli) from Al-Sindi ibn Al-Rabi' from Uthman ibn Isa from Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him, saying to him: 'My brother married a woman and she bore him children. Then my brother's wife went and breastfed a girl from among the people. Is it permissible for me to marry that girl whom my brother's wife breastfed?' He said: 'No, indeed, what becomes prohibited through breastfeeding is what becomes prohibited through lineage.'

key_terms.الرَّضَاع: Breastfeeding (the act of nursing an infant)
key_terms.عُرْض: People / Public (referring to the general population)

ai.seo_question: Does breastfeeding by a brother's wife make her child my milk sister?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the prohibition of marriage through breastfeeding (Rada') is equivalent in strength to that of blood lineage (Nasab), a principle derived from the Quranic verse 'And breastfeeding mothers should nurse their children for two complete years.' This ruling establishes that the wife of one's brother becomes a milk mother to any child she nurses, thereby making her milk-daughter a permanent mahram to the brother, mirroring the status of a full sister. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining kinship ties beyond biological descent, emphasizing the spiritual and legal weight of the nursing bond.
